idiom_name: two plain objects/typed arrays + destructuring swap of the references
implementation_notes: In the event loop a single assignment is atomic, so the pattern reduces to two plain buffers and one swapped variable: the writer fills `next`, then `[current, next] = [next, current]` publishes it, and readers (a render pass, a `requestAnimationFrame` callback, a worker message handler) always read `current` and can never observe a partially built frame. Because one agent has no threads, no lock or atomic API is needed - the discipline is to write only into `next` and never touch `current` after the swap. Across agents use `postMessage` with transferable `ArrayBuffer`s, or `SharedArrayBuffer` + `Atomics` when the same memory must be observed by several threads.
pitfalls: The swap is atomic for the reference only: mutating `current.entities` after publishing is the torn-state bug in JavaScript clothing.
Objects handed to a worker are structured-cloned (or transferred); a `SharedArrayBuffer` is the only memory two agents can both see, and only `Atomics` operations on it are race-free.
GC hides lifetime bugs: keeping the old frame referenced prevents reuse, and dropping it mid-render can hand the writer a buffer a callback still expects.

variants.name: OffscreenCanvas back buffer presented as ImageBitmap
variants.implementation_notes: For explicit rendering double buffering, draw the whole scene into an `OffscreenCanvas` (it may live in a worker, reached via `transferControlToOffscreen()`) and present the finished frame by transferring it: `transferToImageBitmap()` detaches the rendered bitmap and an `ImageBitmapRenderingContext` obtained from the visible canvas renders it with `transferFromImageBitmap(bitmap)`. This is the browser analogue of a page flip - the visible surface only receives complete frames and expensive composition stays off the critical path. Browsers already double-buffer ordinary canvas rendering, so use this variant only when an explicit back buffer is genuinely needed.
pitfalls: `transferToImageBitmap()` detaches the OffscreenCanvas contents: re-initialize before drawing the next frame, or alternate two offscreen canvases.
A `bitmaprenderer` context cannot be mixed with drawing calls on the same canvas - use separate elements or an OffscreenCanvas as the production surface.
Worker rendering needs the canvas transferred with `transferControlToOffscreen()` first; a detached or closed OffscreenCanvas silently stops producing frames.
